importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — container home, PUF panel house, wooden cottage, A-frame, and capsule house are visually distinct product types. Buyers use the image to confirm product type before reading any text; wrong visual type causes an immediate skip.

Floor area, structure material, wall panel type, and number of floors are non-interchangeable shortlisting criteria. A buyer needing a 1000 sq ft steel-frame PUF panel house cannot evaluate a listing without these specs.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per sq ft dominates for custom residential builds; per unit applies to standard fixed-configuration houses; per project applies to labour colonies and multi-unit institutional orders. All three conventions are active in the Indian market — price cannot be compared without unit clarity.
importance_ranking.reason: Per unit vs per sq ft vs per project are all live quoting conventions in this category. A buyer comparing prices across listings cannot interpret or compare any price figure without knowing the unit basis.

Indian buyers are price-sensitive but price is only comparable after floor area and structure type are confirmed — a per-sq-ft rate for a PUF panel house is not comparable to one for a precast concrete structure. Listed price is a budget entry point; final price is always negotiated and site-specific.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with universal buyer recall exists — EPACK, Tata Nest-In, and Synergy are trade-known but buyers search by product type and configuration, not manufacturer name. No branded sub-categories appear in taxonomy siblings.
importance_ranking.reason: Manufacturer track record, BMTPC PAC certification, and service location coverage are genuine buyer qualifiers for a high-value, site-delivered product — but company ranks last because spec and visual fit must be confirmed first.
